name: Basic Beans and Rice
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) cooked black or pinto beans, drained
steps: Cook rice by basic method.
When rice is tender, gently stir in drained beans, oil, garlic and cumin.
Cover and warm 3–5 minutes until beans hot. Serve
notes: Swap: Any cooked canned beans; canned corn or peas for extra vegetables
Why it helps: Energy from rice plus protein/fiber from beans
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Red Lentil Tomato Stew
ingredients: ¾ cup dry split red lentils
steps: Sort and rinse lentils.
Simmer lentils in water 10 minutes.
Add tomatoes and seasonings.
Simmer another 5–10 minutes until fully soft; add water if thick
notes: Swap: Replace tomatoes with 1 can mixed vegetables and a pinch of salt
Why it helps: Protein, fiber and some vegetables in one pot
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: One-Pot Lentil Rice Pilaf
ingredients: ¾ cup dry white long-grain rice
3½ cups potable water total (plus extra if needed)
steps: Sort and rinse lentils.
Simmer lentils in 2 cups water for 10–15 minutes.
Add rice and remaining 1½ cups water; bring back to boil.
Cover, lower heat and simmer 15–20 minutes until both rice and lentils are tender; add a small splash of water if needed.
Rest covered 5 minutes, then season
notes: Note: Stoves and varieties differ: if lentils remain firm when rice is nearly done, add a little water and continue; do not serve hard lentils
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Three-Bean Pantry Chili
ingredients: 3 cans (15 oz each) different cooked beans, drained
steps: Combine all ingredients in pot.
Bring to a bubbling simmer, stirring.
Simmer 8–10 minutes until heated through and flavors combine
notes: Swap: One or two bean cans can be replaced with canned lentils or vegetables
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Tuna and Pea Rice Bowl
steps: Cook rice.
Stir in peas and tuna; warm thoroughly for 2–3 minutes.
Season to taste
notes: Swap: Canned salmon or canned chicken instead of tuna. Be mindful of fish intake recommendations, particularly for pregnancy/children
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Peanut Butter Banana Oatmeal
ingredients: ½ banana (fresh or shelf-stable freeze-dried), optional cinnamon
steps: Cook oats in water until creamy.
Turn off heat and stir in peanut butter.
Top with banana/cinnamon
notes: Swap: Raisins instead of banana; sunflower-seed butter if peanuts are unsuitable
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Savory Vegetable Oats
steps: Heat water and oats until mostly softened.
Stir in vegetables and seasonings.
Simmer a couple more minutes until hot
notes: Note: Check bouillon sodium and adjust to available diet needs
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Tomato Chickpea Couscous
ingredients: 1 cup boiling potable water (or package amount)
steps: Bring measured water to boil, turn heat off.
Stir in instant couscous, cover and stand according to package (typically 5 min).
Fluff and fold in chickpeas, tomatoes and garlic.
Warm briefly if desired; eat promptly
notes: Note: Use instant couscous, not uncooked whole wheat berries or large pearl couscous
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Sardine and Tomato Pasta
ingredients: ½ can diced tomatoes or tomato sauce
steps: Cook pasta per package and carefully drain.
Stir in tomato and sardines over low heat until warmed through.
Season
notes: Swap: Canned salmon or white beans for sardines
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Canned Vegetable Noodle Soup
ingredients: ½–1 tsp low-sodium bouillon (adjust per label)
½ can cooked white beans, optional
steps: Bring seasoned water to boil.
Add pasta and cook to package directions.
Add canned vegetables and beans for final 3–4 minutes; heat thoroughly
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Chickpea Peanut Stew
steps: Warm chickpeas, tomatoes, cumin and ½ cup water to simmer.
Mix peanut butter with a little hot liquid in a bowl until smooth, then stir into pot.
Simmer 5 minutes, adding a little water as needed
notes: Safety: Clearly tag peanuts as a major allergen
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Quick Black Bean Corn Skillet
steps: Combine all in pan.
Stir over medium heat for 5–8 minutes until hot.
Eat alone or wrap in shelf-stable tortillas
notes: Swap: Pinto beans, peas or canned carrots
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Split Pea Soup
steps: Sort and rinse peas.
Bring peas and water to boil.
Lower heat and simmer, lid ajar, until peas become fully soft (often 40–60 minutes, sometimes more).
Add water as needed, stir frequently near end.
Season
notes: Note: Very old split peas can take longer. This is not a low-fuel meal
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Rice and Tomato Soup
ingredients: ½ cup uncooked long-grain white rice
steps: Bring water to boil, add rice and cover loosely at simmer.
After about 12 minutes add tomatoes and beans.
Simmer until rice is tender, 5–10 minutes more; add water for soup consistency
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Instant Mashed Potato Bean Bowl
ingredients: ½ can canned peas or corn
steps: Heat water per potato package and prepare flakes.
In same pot (before adding flakes) warm beans and vegetables in the water if amount permits, then stir in flakes; alternatively warm canned foods separately.
Season and serve
notes: Note: Some potato mixes require milk/butter; buy a just-add-water variety or follow package adaptations
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: No-Cook Chickpea and Corn Salad
water: 0 cups if using clean ready-to-eat canned ingredients
steps: Open and drain canned foods safely.
Mix with oil and optional acid/seasoning.
Eat immediately
notes: Note: Drain with clean utensils; rinse only if potable rinse water is available. After opening, leftovers require safe refrigeration
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: No-Cook Tuna and White Bean Bowl
steps: Open cans and drain.
Combine, season and eat immediately. Use crackers if available
notes: Note: Tuna is cooked in the can; observe allergen and fish-intake considerations. No safe refrigerator means no storage of opened leftovers
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: No-Cook Overnight Oats (ONLY WITH REFRIGERATION)
water: ½–¾ cup potable water or milk
ingredients: ½–¾ cup potable water or shelf-stable milk
steps: Mix in clean jar.
Refrigerate until softened (typically overnight).
Eat cold
notes: Critical warning: NOT appropriate for unrefrigerated overnight storage during a power outage. Do not display this in the no-refrigeration recipe filter. For no-power conditions, use hot oats or immediately mixed oats if the product is labeled ready to eat without cooking
Use oats specifically labeled suitable for uncooked refrigerated preparation. Keep the jar at 40°F / 4°C or below throughout; an unpowered refrigerator is not automatically safe.
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Instant Oat Peanut Butter Snack Bowl
fuel: none if safe ready-to-eat instant oats and potable water are used
ingredients: 1 instant oatmeal packet labeled suitable for adding water
steps: Prepare oats according to package. If hot water is required, heat it safely.
Stir in peanut butter and raisins.
Eat immediately
notes: Note: Do not assume all raw oat products can be eaten uncooked; follow manufacturer directions
Default filter treats this as needing heat. Only use cold preparation when the exact product explicitly permits it; adding water alone is not a ready-to-eat claim.

name: Campfire Foil-Free Potato and Bean Pot
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes cut into small cubes
steps: Build an outdoor cooking fire and wait for a stable cooking bed; never place an unsafe pot on unstable flames.
Bring potable water to simmer in fire-safe pot.
Add diced potatoes and cook until fork-tender, about 12–20 minutes depending on size.
Drain excess water safely.
Add beans, vegetables and spices; heat 3–5 minutes and serve
notes: Safety: Campfires are subject to local burn bans. Use gloves/tools and never leave fire unattended. Extinguish completely after use
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Quick Red Lentil Curry over Couscous
water: 2½ cups for lentils plus couscous package amount
ingredients: ½ cup instant couscous plus its required hot water
steps: Sort/rinse lentils and simmer in 2½ cups water until soft, about 10–15 minutes.
Add tomatoes and curry powder, simmer 3–5 minutes.
Separately prepare instant couscous using boiling water per package.
Spoon lentils over couscous
notes: Swap: Use instant rice instead of couscous, prepared per package
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Canned Salmon Potato Chowder (No Milk)
steps: Simmer potato in water until completely fork-tender, about 12–20 minutes.
Mash some potato against pot to thicken.
Stir in corn and canned salmon.
Simmer 3–5 minutes until hot. Season
notes: Note: Canned salmon can contain soft edible bones; check label and use care for vulnerable eaters
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Low-Water Tomato White Bean Couscous
water: up to 1 cup, adjust to couscous package and tomato liquid
ingredients: potable water as needed to meet couscous package liquid amount
steps: Measure tomato liquid and add enough potable water so total liquid meets couscous package requirement (the tomatoes contain both liquid and solids; err on side of a little extra liquid).
Bring tomatoes, liquid and beans to a boil.
Turn heat off, stir in instant couscous, cover and stand as directed by package.
Fluff; if still firm, add a little hot water and allow to stand longer
notes: Note: Packaged couscous ratios vary; keep liquid adjustment explicit
source: User cooking pack · original practical recipe

name: Emergency Rice Porridge (Congee-Style)
ingredients: ½ can cooked peas or carrots
steps: Bring rice and water to boil.
Lower to a gentle simmer, partially cover and stir occasionally 40–60 minutes until grains break down into a porridge, adding water as needed.
Stir in canned vegetables at the end, heat and serve
notes: Note: Water- and fuel-intensive. Not the first option during severe shortages, but useful for a soft-texture meal
